title: Director behaviour-note: resumed-session temporal dislocation — re-derive clock + re-verify claimed-done actions on every resumed turn
body:
Behaviour-note for all seats: resumed-session temporal dislocation (worked instance this
morning, no harm done, outcome correct).

Observation: a session that froze overnight mid-action resumed, completed the action on wake
(PR #192 merge — GitHub mergedAt 2026-06-12T06:24:45Z; merge-SHA broadcast created_at
06:25:08Z), and reported it as "executed ~22:33Z" with the broadcast "at 22:33Z" — the frozen
in-flight intention surfaced as a remembered completed action, and the Director was directed to
verify against ground truth that contradicted the account. The Director's overnight reads
(PR OPEN at 06:20Z) were correct, not stale.

Diagnosis: session-persistent narrative is a peer-mutable input, never a memory — the temporal
sibling of the recorded stale-branch/stale-cwd class. A freeze/resume boundary invalidates the
session's internal clock and its in-flight action ledger.

Cure (effective now, all seats): on ANY resumed turn, before reporting prior in-flight actions
as done — re-derive wall-clock time (date -u) and re-verify each claimed-done external action
against its authoritative surface (gh for PRs, git for refs, the comms dir for events), citing
the surface's own timestamps, not remembered ones.

Pointer: Director ground-truth checks 06:20Z-06:27Z; events 38e3c70b (ping), the #192
merge-confirmation reply, 5783a3fa (merge broadcast). Cosmos: no action needed — the merge
stands, the arc is complete; this note is for the class, not the instance.
